blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Google's 'Hybrid Research Model' as a novel approach to integrating research with product development, emphasizing the embedding of research activities within product teams to minimize technology transfer challenges. The model leverages Google's large-scale infrastructure and user base to conduct 'in vivo' research, where ideas are tested through production or near-production code from day one. Colyer appreciates the iterative, data-driven nature of the approach, which ensures research aligns with real-world constraints and user benefits. He also notes the model's flexibility, allowing teams to balance research and engineering as needed, and its emphasis on diverse knowledge dissemination beyond traditional peer-reviewed papers.

Introduction

In this paper, we describe how we organize Computer Science (CS) research at Google. We focus on how we
integrate research and development (R&D) and discuss the benefits and risks of our approach.
